audience.programmeDescription: This mainly Dutch-taught bachelor studies child and adolescent development, upbringing and ways to support children, families and communities.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Utrecht combines a 135 EC major with 45 EC of profiling electives. The UCR options emphasize development in social settings, mental health and assessment, or children and public policy.

cellNotes.text: Utrecht studies infancy and childhood in family and other caregiving settings. The UCR plans approach early development through lifespan psychology.
Both study childhood and adolescence. The UCR course also covers adulthood and ageing.
A recommended first-year major elective linked to Utrecht’s Pedagogical Practicum.
Both examine mental health conditions and risk factors. Utrecht focuses on development.
Both examine assessment and interpretation. Utrecht applies them to parenting and developmental difficulties.
Utrecht studies the selection and evaluation of interventions for children and families.
Choose Testing and Observation Skills for the clinical child and family path or Doing a Qualitative Research Project for the youth, education and society path.
Both consider young people in settings affected by social division. The UCR course focuses on resilience to extremism.
Utrecht connects cultural diversity to parenting and development. UCR examines social differences across sociology, psychology and media courses.
A shared elective in both study paths that examines parenting in its social context.
Utrecht combines pedagogical policy with evaluation of interventions. UCR develops general policy analysis and research skills.
Both introduce research design, measurement and statistics.
Both apply quantitative methods to behavioral research.
Utrecht requires advanced pedagogical methods before the thesis. UCR’s advanced methods course focuses on systematic reviews and meta-analysis.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC thesis after three methods courses. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled degree.
Choose 45 EC of electives for depth or breadth. At least 15 EC must be at intermediate level or higher. In this example, at least 7.5 EC must be advanced.
Both examine ethical judgments. Utrecht applies ethics and the philosophy of science to pedagogical practice.
A shared elective that practises professional conversations with children and adults.

notes.text: Utrecht teaches pedagogical practice through a first-year project, child and family assessment, intervention study and a required thesis. The UCR plans offer foundations in development, mental health or policy. Child-focused diagnostic practice and supervised clinical training require separate study.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.text: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

BENECON311.text: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.text: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
